findings.issue_text: Migration dereferences the first result of embed_category and uncategorized_category_id queries without handling missing rows, causing deployment-blocking crashes when default settings have no database rows
Migration inserts existing host values without hostname normalization, so previously supported values containing schemes or paths will no longer match after migration
Migration interpolates administrator-controlled host values directly into SQL, allowing quotes to break the migration and potentially enabling SQL injection during deployment
EmbeddableHost validation calls sub! on host without handling null values, causing NoMethodError and a 500 response instead of a validation error
record_for_host compares lower(host) with a non-lowercased URI hostname, incorrectly rejecting valid mixed-case DNS hostnames
Validation permits ports, but record_for_host compares stored host-and-port values against URI#host without the port, so configured hosts containing ports never match
Normalized hosts lack a uniqueness validation or database constraint, allowing duplicates with conflicting categories and nondeterministic topic assignment
Model hydration calls .map on every *_ids value without checking for null, causing nullable to-many relationships to throw and prevent model loading
Admin embeddable host update and destroy actions do not handle unknown IDs, invoking methods on nil and returning 500 instead of 404

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation permits ports, but record_for_host compares stored host-and-port values against URI#host without the port, so configured hosts containing ports never match

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model validates hosts with a regex that permits ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), and the before_validation strips the protocol and path but preserves the port in the stored host value. However, in record_for_host method, it extracts uri.host (which returns just the hostname without port) and compares it against the stored host value using 'where("lower(host) = ?", host)'. If a host was configured with a port like 'example.com:8080', the stored value would be 'example.com:8080', but uri.host would return just 'example.com', causing the comparison to fail. This is a real bug where hosts configured with ports would never match incoming requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Normalized hosts lack a uniqueness validation or database constraint, allowing duplicates with conflicting categories and nondeterministic topic assignment

adjudication.rationale: The finding is valid. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) only has a format validation for the host field but no uniqueness validation. The migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) creates the table without a unique index on the host column. The record_for_host method uses `.first` which would return an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. This could lead to nondeterministic category assignment when embedding topics, as TopicEmbed.import uses EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) to determine the category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Model hydration calls .map on every *_ids value without checking for null, causing nullable to-many relationships to throw and prevent model loading

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in store.js.es6, the new code for handling *_ids relationships does `obj[k].map(function(id) {...})` without checking if obj[k] is null or undefined. If a model has a nullable to-many relationship where the *_ids field is null, calling .map() on null will throw a TypeError. The original code only handled singular *_id fields, but the new code assumes all *_ids values are arrays. This is a real bug that would cause crashes when loading models with null to-many relationships.
